text: May 6th is inextricably linked to our respect and gratitude to the Bulgarian invincible army, said Patriarch Daniil (06.05.2026 10:54)

In the tradition of Bulgarian statehood and churchhood, May 6 is inextricably linked to our respect and gratitude to the Bulgarian invincible army. This was said by the Bulgarian Patriarch and Metropolitan of Sofia Daniil, who today led the solemn blessing of water with the consecration of the battle flags in the capital.

"In unchanging testimony to the triumph of life that came with the Resurrection of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, I wholeheartedly congratulate you on the most holy feast of the holy and glorious Great Martyr George - a wonderful warrior of Christ in faith and virtues and our world-famous heavenly intercessor and miracle worker. Following the tradition of May 6, on the feast day of Saint George the Victorious, our holy Orthodox Church consecrates the banners of the military glory of our victorious Army, imploring God's mercy and protection for our Orthodox army, which preserves the peace and security of our dear homeland and with a sense of duty watches over the life and honor of Bulgarian citizens," Patriarch Daniel also said.

In his words, "our prayers and the sacred acts prescribed on today's feast day have their basis in the historically attested truth that in our centuries-old Orthodox tradition, the trust of the Bulgarian army has always been in God first and foremost - in the One from Whom we know that all real strength and power comes, as well as in our faith in Christ the Savior, which was a leading conviction not only for the warrior and martyr of Christ, Saint George, commemorated today by the Holy Church, but also for all Bulgarian soldiers who entered battle in defense of their brothers and sisters in faith and lineage."

"The sources for the thousand-year history of our people tell us that the tradition of consecrating battle flags dates back to the First Bulgarian Kingdom, from the time of the glorious Bulgarian Tsar Simeon the Great. The first such historically attested event is the consecration, which took place in 917 - before the victorious battle of the Bulgarian weapons at the Aheloy River. In performing this ritual, the strength of our great ancestors' trust in God and His eternal righteousness is revealed before us; their confidence that without God and the gracious power coming from Him to people, we cannot do anything that is truly good and useful. Our Lord Jesus Christ tells us the same thing: "... he who abides in Me, and I in him, he bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing," recalled Patriarch Daniel.

"Guided by this faith and this conviction, our great ancestors of all times have sought and asked for God's help in every endeavor. We do the same today, when in unity and unanimity of Church and state we implore God's help for our glorious army, peace, light and prosperity for our people and homeland. May the sprinkling of these battle banners with water sanctified by God's grace be yet another testimony to our faith in God and a visible sign of God's favor and God's protection for our entire people and especially for the Bulgarian military personnel who have dedicated their lives to sacrificial military service in the ranks of the Bulgarian Army," said the Bulgarian Patriarch.
